we have derived the exact analytical solution of a generalized Ginzburg-Landau equation for a one dimensional superconductor containing normal layers.
the introduction of three $\delta$-functions in the modified stationary GL-equation leads to an exact solution of the boundary value problem.

(a) the critical current density is a bifurcation point for the modified GL equation and (b) the critical current is proportional to $\delta$ and to the ratio of the superconducting and normal layer thicknesses.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a model of a superconductor containing normal layers.
a model for the superconductor/insulator/superconductor (SIS) sandwich structure and with the solution of the nonlinear boundary-value problem.
the study of a superconductor-normal-superconductor structure.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the critical current $j_c$ in the one-dimensional superconducting-normal layer-superconducting structure can be determined analytically by using the generalized Ginzburg-Landau model.

the Josephson critical current density $j_{cJ} = 2 \Delta_0/\Phi_0 \approx 0.5 \times 10^8 \mbox{A}/\mbox{cm}^2$, which is the value for a bulk superconductor, is reduced to a value $j_c \approx 0$ when the thickness of the sandwich layer is small enough, i.e. when the normal layer is thin.
the introduction of three $\delta$-functions of appropriate strength in the generalized GL model leads to an analytical solution of the boundary-value problem for the modified stationary GL-equation.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the modified GL equation provides a simple and efficient tool in the study of the Josephson effect for a one-dimensional Josephson junction. [1]
the critical current density is proportional to the square root of the normal layer thickness.

the introduction of a sandwich layer of thickness $d$ leads to an increase of the critical current density by a factor of $1/\cosh(d/\lambda)$, where $\lambda$ is the penetration depth of the superconductor.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the critical Josephion current $j_c$ is proportional to the thickness $d$ of the normal layer.
the introduction of the normal layer leads to a significant reduction of the critical Josephson-current density $j_c$, and that $j_c$ depends on the thickness of the sandwich layer.
the introduction of $\delta$-functions in the GL model allows one to derive an exact analytical solution for the current density-phase offset relationship.
